findings.title: `totalPages` is off by one when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.description: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` yields 2 pages for 50 members at limit 50 (and 3 for 100). `showingLast` is then false on the real last page, so `next` (lines 29-38) sets `offset` to `user_count` and loads an empty page shown as "2/2". The same empty page appears after removing the only member on a trailing page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Re-adding an existing member raises a 500 and leaves the batch half-applied
findings.description:
`group.add(user)` is `users.push(user)` (`app/models/group.rb:272-274`), which inserts a `group_users` row immediately on a persisted group. `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)` (`db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9`), so an existing member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no transaction, so users earlier in the list stay added while the request fails.

This is easy to hit from the new UI: the input is never cleared (`// TODO` at `admin-group.js.es6:62`), so a second click on "Add" resends the same usernames. The old `usernames=` path diffed against current members and did not have this problem. Skip existing members (e.g. filter by `group.users.where(...)`) and wrap the loop in a transaction.

findings.title: Removing a member no longer clears the user's `primary_group_id`
findings.description:
The old path went through `Group#usernames=` and `destroy_deletions`, which nulls `primary_group_id` for removed users (`app/models/group.rb:287-295`). The new `group.users.delete(user_id)` bypasses that, and `GroupUser` has no callbacks (`app/models/group_user.rb`). A removed user keeps the group as primary, and `PostSerializer` (`app/serializers/post_serializer.rb:97-103`) keeps showing that group name on their posts.

Two related points I could not confirm by reading alone:
- **Counter cache:** a has-many-through `delete` removes join rows with `delete_all`, so the `user_count` counter cache on `GroupUser` may not be decremented. The spec only asserts `group.users.count`, not `user_count`.
- **Non-member id:** deleting an id that is not a member will likely raise `RecordNotFound` rather than "succeed silently" as the removed spec required.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncates at 50 members
findings.description: `GroupsController#members` now always paginates with a default limit of 50 (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26`). Previously non-automatic groups returned every member and automatic groups returned 200. The public template (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6`) renders `members` with no pager or load-more, so members past the first 50 are unreachable there. Paging controls exist only in the admin template. Also, `{{#if model}}` on line 1 of that template is now always true, since the model is the group rather than the member array.

findings.title: `limit` and `offset` on the public members endpoint are unvalidated
findings.description:
`limit` and `offset` are taken from params with only `.to_i`, on an endpoint reachable by any user who can see the group.
- A negative value reaches `.limit()`/`.offset()` and will error in PostgreSQL (500).
- An arbitrarily large `limit` removes the pagination bound.
- `limit=0` is echoed back in `meta.limit` and stored on the model (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:33`), after which the `currentPage`/`totalPages` divisions produce `NaN`/`Infinity`.

Clamp to a range, e.g. `limit.clamp(1, MAX)` and `[offset, 0].max`.

findings.title: Add and remove member requests have no failure handling in the client
findings.description: `removeMember` and `addMembers` chain only a success callback, and the controller actions (`admin-group.js.es6:51-65`) add no rejection handler. A 422 from `can_not_modify_automatic` or the 500 described above gives the admin no feedback. The `save` and `destroy` actions in the same controller both show a `bootbox.alert` on failure. Unknown usernames are also skipped silently server-side (`groups_controller.rb:72`) while the response reports success.

findings.title: Test coverage shrank and the new pagination contract is untested
findings.description:
- **Removed cases not replaced:** adding a non-existent user, removing a non-member, and updating or renaming a non-automatic group.
- **Missing new cases:** adding an already-present member (the 500 path above) and `user_count` / `primary_group_id` after removal.
- **Wrong verb:** line 115 calls `remove_member` with `xhr :put` although the route is `DELETE` (`config/routes.rb:49`).
- **Seeded ids:** lines 52, 94 and 115 rely on group id `1`, whereas the `.destroy` spec uses `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`.
- **Stale pending spec:** the pagination spec at `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb:72-85` is still `pending` with the comment "until we fix group truncation". It also still parses the response as a bare array, though the endpoint now returns `{members:, meta:}`. Nothing exercises the new shape, `meta.total`, or the default limit.

findings.title: New JavaScript violates the project's JSHint settings
findings.description:
`.jshintrc` sets `"eqeqeq": true`, but lines 7 and 12 use `== 0`. In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`:
- **Line 59:** missing semicolon after `})`.
- **Line 82:** `{ return };` puts the semicolon outside the block.
- **Line 21:** `findMembers` now returns `undefined` on an empty name, where it previously returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. The method returns a promise on one path and nothing on the other, and the `next`/`previous` actions return that value.

findings.title: Model code left without a production caller
findings.description: After this change `Group#usernames=` and its `destroy_deletions` hook (lines 286-295) are referenced only from specs (`spec/models/group_spec.rb:149,153`, `spec/models/user_spec.rb:1011,1022`). `Group#remove` (lines 276-278) has no caller I could find; the new `remove_member` action does not use it either. Either route the controller through these methods, which would also restore the `primary_group_id` cleanup, or remove them.

findings.title: Admin and public group API contracts changed without a compatibility path
findings.description:
- `create` and `update` now read top-level `name` / `visible` / `alias_level` instead of `group[...]`.
- The `PATCH` `changes: {add, delete}` membership API is removed.
- `GET /groups/:name/members` changed from an array to `{members, meta}`.

In-repo callers were updated (the only `findMembers` consumer is `group.js`), but external API clients and plugins using the old shapes will break without a clear error. For example, a `group[name]` create now fails name validation on an empty string.

findings.title: New group styles use hard-coded colours and `!important`
findings.description: `.next, .previous` use literal `#333` / `#aaa` with `!important`, and `.ac-wrap` overrides use `!important`. These are the only occurrences of those literals in the file, so they will not follow colour-scheme customisation.

findings.title: New membership endpoints are correctly restricted and wired
findings.description: `add_members` and `remove_member` live in `Admin::GroupsController` (inherits `Admin::AdminController`), and their routes sit under `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (`config/routes.rb:45-51`). Both use `params.require` and reject automatic groups with a 422 before mutating. The `ILIKE` search stays parameterised. The i18n keys the new templates use (`delete_member_confirm`, `name`, `add`, `add_members`) exist in `config/locales/client.en.yml:1630-1633`, and the `group-member` view's `templateName` follows the existing `admin/templates/...` convention.
